origin: From the preset buttons on old car radios: pressing one popped out the one already pressed, so only one was ever down. That behavior became the name.
whenToUse: There are two to five options that need comparing.
Each option needs a note, such as a price or period.
One option must be chosen (a default can be preselected).
whenNotToUse: There are many options (use a select or a combobox).
A single setting that turns on and off (use a switch).

alternatives.name: Segmented Control
alternatives.reason: Two to four short options that change the view.

accessibility: Group it with fieldset and legend so the question is read along with the options.
Native radio inputs let the arrow keys move between options while Tab passes the group in one step.
The whole card is the label, so the pressable area is large.
The selected state shows with a filled radio mark, not only a border color.
